items.pronunciation_notes: Breathy bh at the front and a throaty kh at the back, with a long uu between: bhuukh.

learn.title_en: मुझे भूख लगी है — hunger has attached to me
learn.explanation_en: There is no Hindi adjective meaning hungry. भूख is a feminine noun and it attaches to you with लगना, exactly as डर and ठंड did: मुझे भूख लगी है. The verb agrees with भूख, so it is लगी and never लगा, whoever is speaking. This is the third time this shape has appeared in Module 8, and it is worth treating as the default for anything your body is doing to you rather than something to relearn each time.

examples.note: लगी agrees with the feminine भूख, not with the speaker.
तुम्हें is तुम with को fused, from Module 6.
The person can be left out entirely when it is obvious.

common_error.why_en: भूखा does exist as an adjective but is much stronger, closer to starving or destitute. For ordinary hunger Hindi uses the noun.

practice.question: भूख
practice.explanation_en: भूख is hunger, and it is feminine.

game.explanation_en: भूख लगना — hunger attaches to you, and the person takes को.

items.pronunciation_notes: One syllable, with the p and y run together as a single cluster: pyaas.

learn.explanation_en: प्यास is thirst, feminine, and it takes लगना just as भूख does. The two are learnt as a pair because they turn up together constantly and behave identically: मुझे भूख लगी है and मुझे प्यास लगी है. That is a useful thing about this construction — once you have it, adding a new body state costs you only the noun. What you cannot do is guess the verb, which is why the game card keeps asking.

examples.note: Identical in shape to the hunger sentence.

examples.english: give me water, I am thirsty
examples.note: दो is the तुम imperative of देना.
The past, and both words are feminine because प्यास is.

common_error.why_en: प्यास is feminine, so the verb is लगी. The consonant ending gives no clue, which is why it is flagged.

practice.question: प्यास
practice.explanation_en: प्यास is thirst, feminine, and it behaves exactly like भूख.

game.explanation_en: प्यास लगना — the same verb as भूख. The two are a pair.

items.pronunciation_notes: The nasal is a hum on the long ii and the द is barely released: niiṁd.

learn.title_en: Sleep comes — it does not attach
learn.explanation_en: This is the item the collocation card exists for. भूख and प्यास take लगना, and नींद — sitting in the same block, describing the same kind of bodily state — takes आना instead. मुझे नींद आ रही है, I am feeling sleepy. There is no reason for the difference and no rule to derive it from; the pairing simply belongs to the word. Note also that नींद is the state of sleepiness, while सोना is the verb for actually sleeping.

examples.note: रही agrees with the feminine नींद.
Literally sleep did not come to me — the standard way to say it.
The verb सोना, for the act rather than the feeling.

common_error.why_en: लगना goes with भूख and प्यास but not with नींद. Sleep comes rather than attaching, and there is no logic behind the split.

practice.question: नींद
practice.explanation_en: नींद is sleep or sleepiness. सोना is the verb for the act of sleeping.

game.explanation_en: नींद आना — sleep comes. This is where it differs from भूख and प्यास.

summary.recap_en: Three body states, one construction, and two different verbs. भूख and प्यास take लगना; नींद takes आना. Nothing predicts which, and that is precisely why the collocation is drilled rather than the gender.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the doctor, injury, and the adjective for feeling weak — completing the health block.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ऑ vowel sign is used only for English loanwords and sounds like the o in 'doctor': ḍaak-ṭar.

learn.title_en: डॉक्टर, and a vowel sign that only English words use
learn.explanation_en: डॉक्टर is borrowed from English, with retroflex ट as loanwords always take and the vowel sign ऑ, which exists in Hindi almost entirely to write English o sounds — डॉक्टर, कॉलेज, ऑफ़िस. It is masculine by default, though a woman doctor is also डॉक्टर and the agreement follows the person. You go to one with के पास, the same phrase Module 6 taught for near and for having.

examples.note: के पास for going to a person, rather than a bare destination.
Professionals usually take plural agreement out of respect, so कहते हैं rather than कहता है.
No word for a is needed, and the noun does not change for a woman.

common_error.why_en: Going to a person takes के पास. को would mark the doctor as an object rather than a destination.

practice.question: डॉक्टर
practice.explanation_en: डॉक्टर is a doctor, and the same word is used for a woman.

game.question_en: Which phrase goes with डॉक्टर when you visit one?
game.explanation_en: डॉक्टर के पास जाना — going to a person uses के पास.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ट is retroflex, made with the tongue curled back: choṭ, one syllable.

learn.title_en: चोट लगना — injury attaches, and nobody is blamed
learn.explanation_en: चोट is an injury, feminine and flagged, and it takes लगना like भूख and प्यास: मुझे चोट लगी, I got hurt. Notice what that construction does not say — it names no cause and no one at fault. Hindi finds this shape natural for accidents, where English would need a passive or a vague subject. If you want to say where, the body part takes में or पर: पैर में चोट लगी.

examples.note: The bare perfective, and लगी agrees with चोट.
With है the result still stands — the injury is current.

examples.english: it is not a bad injury
examples.note: ज़्यादा means much or excessive, and नहीं sits in front of the verb.

common_error.why_en: चोट is feminine, so the perfective is लगी. This is the same agreement as भूख लगी and प्यास लगी.

practice.question: चोट
practice.explanation_en: चोट is an injury, feminine, and it attaches with लगना.

game.explanation_en: चोट लगना — the injury attaches, and no one is named as the cause.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted ज़ is a z, so the middle of the word buzzes: kam-zor.

learn.title_en: कमज़ोर — one form, and it covers more than the body
learn.explanation_en: कमज़ोर is weak, unmarked so it never changes, and built from two Persian pieces — कम meaning less and ज़ोर meaning force. It describes bodies, but also arguments, signals and excuses, exactly as weak does in English. Its opposite is मज़बूत, strong, which is also unmarked. Both are worth learning together, and neither will ever ask you to choose an ending.

examples.note: The adjective is identical whoever is speaking.
A feminine subject, and still कमज़ोर.

examples.hindi: बुख़ार के बाद कमज़ोरी आती है
examples.read_as: bukhaar ke baad kamzorii aatii hai
examples.note: कमज़ोरी is the noun, formed with -ी exactly as ख़ुशी was from ख़ुश.

common_error.why_en: कमज़ोरी is the noun weakness. The adjective is कमज़ोर, and adding -ी makes it a different word rather than a feminine form.

practice.question: कमज़ोर
practice.explanation_en: कमज़ोर is weak, and it never changes its form.

game.explanation_en: कमज़ोर होना. Adjectives of state take होना; it is the nouns that vary.

tts_strings: बुख़ार के बाद कमज़ोरी आती है

summary.recap_en: The health block is complete at twelve words. Almost all of it runs on one construction — the state is the subject, the person takes को — and the only thing that varies is which verb each noun happens to take. Adjectives of state are the exception and all take होना.
summary.next_up_en: Next: work and the office, starting with the noun the collocation card was designed around.

items.pronunciation_notes: One long syllable, and the m is fully closed at the end: kaam.
items.gloss_en: work, a task, a job to be done

learn.explanation_en: काम is work, and काम करना is to work. That looks obvious until you notice how many English verbs Hindi could have chosen — make, do, take — and how confidently learners reach for बनाना, to make, because English says make a living and do the work interchangeably. It is करना, always. काम is also a countable task: बहुत काम है means there is a lot to do, and मेरा एक काम है means I have something to attend to.

examples.note: The habitual present — करना is transitive, so the perfective waits for Module 9.

examples.english: there is a lot of work
examples.note: काम as a countable task, with a singular verb.
होना rather than करना, because nobody is named as the doer.

common_error.why_en: बनाना is to make or build something. Work is done rather than made, and this is the pairing the whole collocation card exists to teach.

practice.question: काम
practice.explanation_en: काम is work or a task, masculine, and unchanged in the plural.

game.explanation_en: काम करना. बनाना means to make something, and it is the commonest wrong guess here.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f and no vowel follows it: daf-tar.

learn.explanation_en: दफ़्तर is an office, a Persian borrowing, masculine and Class 2. The English ऑफ़िस is equally common in speech and neither is more correct — दफ़्तर is slightly more formal and turns up in writing, ऑफ़िस is what many people actually say. Like any destination with जाना, it takes no postposition: दफ़्तर जाओ, go to the office. But with में it means inside: दफ़्तर में काम है.

examples.note: The destination takes no postposition, as always with जाना.

examples.english: there is a lot of work at the office
examples.note: में for being inside, and दफ़्तर is oblique before it.
बंद is unmarked and means closed or shut.

common_error.why_en: जाना takes its destination bare. Adding को is a translation of the English to.

practice.question: दफ़्तर
practice.explanation_en: दफ़्तर is an office. ऑफ़िस is the equally common English borrowing.

game.explanation_en: दफ़्तर जाना — and the destination takes no postposition.

items.pronunciation_notes: The first syllable holds a diphthong close to the vowel in English 'now': nau-krii.

learn.explanation_en: काम is work in general — the task in front of you. नौकरी is a job in the employment sense, the post you hold and get paid for. So काम करना is to be working and नौकरी करना is to be employed, and नौकरी ढूँढ़ना is job-hunting. नौकरी is feminine and predictable from its -ी ending, declining like लड़की, so नौकरियों में in the oblique plural.

examples.note: करता agrees with the subject, not with नौकरी.
अच्छी is feminine, agreeing with नौकरी.
उसकी is feminine, agreeing with the thing possessed as Module 6 taught.

common_error.why_en: नौकरी ends in -ी and is feminine, so the adjective takes -ी too.

practice.question: नौकरी
practice.explanation_en: नौकरी is a job in the employment sense. काम is work in general.

game.explanation_en: नौकरी करना — to hold a job, the same verb as काम.

summary.recap_en: काम is work in general and नौकरी is the job you are employed in — both take करना. दफ़्तर takes जाना with no postposition, exactly as any destination does. काम बनाना is the wrong guess this block exists to prevent.
summary.next_up_en: Next: effort, time off, and the phone — three things every working day runs on.

items.pronunciation_notes: The ह is a light breath and the middle vowel almost disappears: meh-nat.

learn.title_en: मेहनत is effort, and it is admired
learn.explanation_en: मेहनत is hard work or effort, feminine and flagged. It is not neutral — calling someone मेहनती, hard-working, is high praise, and मेहनत करो is what a parent or teacher says with real weight behind it. There is no exact English single word: graft comes close in register. The noun is uncountable, so it has no plural, and मेहनती is the adjective formed from it with the same -ी that made ख़ुशी from ख़ुश.

examples.note: करता agrees with the subject, not with मेहनत.
The तुम imperative, and a sentence with a lot of cultural weight.

examples.english: it takes a lot of effort
examples.note: The noun standing alone with होना.

common_error.why_en: Effort is something you put in rather than something that happens to you, so this noun takes करना.

practice.question: मेहनत
practice.explanation_en: मेहनत is hard work or effort, feminine, and it carries real approval.

game.explanation_en: मेहनत करना — effort is put in, not received.

items.pronunciation_notes: Aspirated chh at the front and a doubled retroflex ट held slightly longer: chhuṭ-ṭii.
items.gloss_en: a holiday, a day off, leave

learn.title_en: छुट्टी covers everything from an afternoon to a term
learn.explanation_en: छुट्टी is time off — a day's leave, a public holiday, or the end of the school day. आज छुट्टी है can mean today is a holiday or we have the day off, and छुट्टी हो गई is what schoolchildren shout when the bell goes. The plural छुट्टियाँ means the holidays as a stretch of time, exactly as गर्मियाँ meant the summer. Feminine, predictable from -ी, and it takes लेना.

examples.note: The noun standing alone with होना.
The future — लेना is transitive, so the perfective waits.
The oblique plural, exactly like गर्मियों में.

common_error.why_en: Leave is taken rather than done. करना is the default guess and it is wrong here.

practice.question: छुट्टी
practice.explanation_en: छुट्टी is a holiday or time off, and its plural means the holidays.

game.explanation_en: छुट्टी लेना — leave is taken, not done.

items.pronunciation_notes: The dotted फ़ is an f, so this is fon rather than phon: one syllable.

learn.title_en: फ़ोन करना, and who you call takes को
learn.explanation_en: फ़ोन is both the object and the call, so फ़ोन करना is to phone someone and मेरा फ़ोन कहाँ है is where is my phone. The person you call takes को: मुझे फ़ोन करो, call me. That is the same को you have been using for people on the receiving end all through this module. फ़ोन आना also exists and means a call came in, with the caller unnamed.

examples.note: The person called takes को, so मुझे.
तुम्हें is तुम with को fused.
आना is intransitive, so the perfective is available.

common_error.why_en: लगाना is used for connecting a call in some contexts, but the ordinary verb for phoning someone is करना.

practice.question: फ़ोन
practice.explanation_en: फ़ोन is both the device and the call, masculine, and written with a dotted फ़.

game.question_en: Which verb goes with फ़ोन when you call someone?
game.explanation_en: फ़ोन करना, and the person you call takes को.

summary.recap_en: करना is the default verb in the work block — काम, नौकरी, मेहनत and फ़ोन all take it — but छुट्टी takes लेना, which is exactly the kind of exception the collocation card is for. Anyone on the receiving end of a phone call takes को.
summary.next_up_en: Next: pay and meetings, and a conversation about what you do for a living.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four sounds crowd together in the middle — न, ख़, व — with no vowels between: tan-khvaah.

learn.title_en: तनख़्वाह मिलना — pay is received, not taken
learn.explanation_en: तनख़्वाह is a salary, feminine and flagged, and its verb is मिलना, to be received or obtained. मुझे तनख़्वाह मिली, I got paid — and मिलना is intransitive, so the perfective is fully available to you. That makes this one of the few work words you can use in the past right now. मिलना is worth knowing well beyond this word: it covers getting anything at all, and it also means to meet someone.

examples.note: मिली agrees with the feminine तनख़्वाह, and मिलना is intransitive.
कम is unmarked and means little or less.
अच्छी is feminine, which is the proof that तनख़्वाह is.

common_error.why_en: Pay is received rather than taken. मिलना is intransitive and needs no ने, which is why this sentence works now and the other does not.

practice.question: तनख़्वाह
practice.explanation_en: तनख़्वाह is a salary, and it is feminine.

game.explanation_en: तनख़्वाह मिलना — pay is received. मिलना is intransitive, so no ने is involved.

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट as in every English loanword, and a nasal before the final g: mii-ṭiṁg.

collocation.english: for a meeting to take place

learn.title_en: An English word that took Hindi gender
learn.explanation_en: मीटिंग is borrowed whole from English and is feminine — which is worth pausing on, because English gives no gender at all and Hindi assigned one anyway. Every borrowed noun does this, and there is no rule: बस is feminine, टिकट is masculine, मीटिंग is feminine. The verb is होना, so मीटिंग होना is for a meeting to happen, and मीटिंग में for during one. The Hindi word बैठक also exists and sounds more formal.

examples.note: हुई is feminine, agreeing with मीटिंग.

examples.english: there will be a meeting tomorrow
examples.note: The presumptive form doubling as the future.
मीटिंग is oblique before में, though nothing visible changes.

common_error.why_en: मीटिंग is feminine in Hindi even though English has no gender at all. Borrowed nouns take a gender on arrival.

practice.question: मीटिंग
practice.explanation_en: मीटिंग is a meeting, and Hindi treats it as feminine.

game.explanation_en: मीटिंग होना — a meeting happens. मीटिंग करना also occurs and means to hold one.

items.pronunciation_notes: The three words run together at conversational speed: kaam kar-te ho.

learn.title_en: The habitual present is what this question needs
learn.explanation_en: तुम कहाँ काम करते हो asks where someone works as a standing fact, so it takes the habitual — not the continuous, which would ask where they are working at this moment. That distinction from Module 7 does real work here, because getting it wrong turns a normal question into an oddly specific one. The third line hangs on gender: नौकरी is feminine, so it is तुम्हारी and कैसी, and the reply picks up अच्छी to match.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: मैं दफ़्तर में काम करता हूँ।
lines.read_as: maiṁ daftar meṁ kaam kartaa huuṁ.

lines.speaker: B
lines.hindi: अच्छी है, लेकिन मेहनत बहुत है।
lines.read_as: achchhii hai, lekin mehnat bahut hai.
lines.english: It is good, but there is a lot of hard work.

common_error.wrong: तुम कहाँ काम कर रहे हो?
common_error.why_en: The continuous asks where they are working right now. For someone's occupation, Hindi uses the habitual.

practice.question: तुम कहाँ काम करते हो?
options: where are you working right now?
options_read_as: where are you working right now?
practice.explanation_en: The habitual present asks about someone's occupation as a standing fact.

game.question_en: Listen to the third line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: नौकरी is feminine, so the question word is कैसी.

tts_strings: मैं दफ़्तर में काम करता हूँ।
अच्छी है, लेकिन मेहनत बहुत है।

summary.recap_en: तनख़्वाह takes मिलना, which is intransitive and therefore usable in the past straight away. मीटिंग is a reminder that every borrowed noun gets a Hindi gender on arrival with no rule behind it — बस feminine, टिकट masculine, मीटिंग feminine.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last of the work block, then school and study.
